summary: The article is largely reliable, accurately reporting key dates for TCS's Q1FY27 results and interim dividend consideration, and providing generally correct information on dividend taxation for Indian residents. However, there are some inaccuracies regarding the TDS threshold for resident individuals and the default TDS rate for NRIs.

claims.claim: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is set to announce its Q1FY27 financial results on July 9, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm TCS board meeting on July 9, 2026, to consider Q1FY27 results.

claims.claim: The company's board will also convene on the same date to consider and potentially declare an interim dividend for shareholders.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm TCS board meeting on July 9, 2026, to consider interim dividend.

claims.claim: The previous quarter (Q4FY26) saw a 12.22% increase in net profit, even as the stock experienced some decline.
claims.note: TCS reported a 12.22% rise in consolidated net profit for Q4 FY26. Several sources also mention a decline in stock value during this period.

claims.claim: Companies are generally required to deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on dividend payments if the dividend amount exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year for resident individuals, as per Section 194 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: While Section 194 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, deals with TDS on dividends for resident shareholders, the threshold for TDS deduction has been revised. From FY 2025-26, TDS applies when total dividends to a resident shareholder exceed ₹10,000 in a financial year, not ₹5,000.

claims.claim: For Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), the tax treatment can be different, often subject to double taxation avoidance agreements (DTAA) between India and their country of residence. NRIs generally face a TDS deduction at a rate of 20% (plus surcharge and cess) on dividend income, unless a lower rate is specified under an applicable DTAA.
claims.note: NRIs generally face a 20% TDS on dividend income, subject to DTAA benefits.

claims.claim: If you provide your Permanent Account Number (PAN), the TDS rate is typically 10%.
claims.note: For resident individuals, if the dividend income exceeds the threshold (₹10,000 from FY 2025-26) and PAN is provided, the TDS rate is 10%.

article_title: TCS Q1FY27 Results & Interim Dividend: What Investors Need to Know
